In algebra, specifically in the theory of [[commutative ring]]s, '''Serre's inequality on height''' states: given a (Noetherian) [[regular ring]] ''A'' and a pair of [[prime ideal]]s <math>\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{q}</math> in it, for each prime ideal <math>\mathfrak r</math> that is a [[minimal prime ideal]] over the sum <math>\mathfrak p + \mathfrak q</math>, the following inequality on [[height of an ideal|height]]s holds:<ref>{{harvnb|Serre|2000|loc=Ch. V, § B.6, Theorem 3.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|1998|loc=§ 20.4.}}</ref>
:<math>\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r) \le \operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p) + \operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q).</math>

Without the assumption on regularity, the inequality can fail; see [[scheme-theoretic intersection#Proper intersection]].

== Sketch of Proof ==
Serre gives the following proof of the inequality, based on the validity of [[Serre's multiplicity conjectures]] for [[formal power series ring]] over a [[completion (ring theory)|complete]] [[discrete valuation ring]].<ref>{{harvnb|Serre|2000|loc=Ch. V, § B. 6.}}</ref>

By replacing <math>A</math> by the localization at <math>\mathfrak r</math>, we assume <math>(A, \mathfrak r)</math> is a local ring. Then the inequality is equivalent to the following inequality: for finite <math>A</math>-modules <math>M, N</math> such that <math>M \otimes_A N</math> has finite length,
:<math>\dim_A M + \dim_A N \le \dim A</math>
where <math>\dim_A M = \dim(A/\operatorname{Ann}_A(M))</math> = the dimension of the support of <math>M</math> and similar for <math>\dim_A N</math>. To show the above inequality, we can assume <math>A</math> is complete. Then by [[Cohen's structure theorem]], we can write <math>A = A_1/a_1 A_1</math> where <math>A_1</math> is a formal [[power series]] ring over a complete discrete valuation ring and <math>a_1</math> is a nonzero element in <math>A_1</math>. Now, an argument with the [[Tor spectral sequence]] shows that <math>\chi^{A_1}(M, N) = 0</math>. Then one of Serre's conjectures says <math>\dim_{A_1} M + \dim_{A_1} N < \dim A_1</math>, which in turn gives the asserted inequality. <math>\square</math>
